root_cause: The LSTM test with non-zero dropout (0.1 and 0.3) produces slightly different numerical outputs between OpenVINO and TensorFlow. LSTM with dropout is inherently stochastic; when dropout is applied during inference with test=False semantics, small floating-point differences in the underlying RNN cell computation can accumulate across time steps. The PR under test (IR FE fix for missing XML attributes) does not touch LSTM or TF frontend code - this is an unrelated pre-existing numerical flakiness in the test that surfaces intermittently.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed TensorFlow Layer Tests job - this is a flaky numerical test unrelated to the PR changes
Consider adding a higher tolerance threshold for the LSTM+dropout test or marking it xfail/skip when dropout is non-zero
The PR changes (IR FE XML deserializer) are unrelated to this failure
prevention_strategies: Mark LSTM tests with non-zero dropout as xfail or increase the numerical tolerance threshold, as non-deterministic dropout makes exact comparison unreliable.
historical_context: This is the first recorded instance of this specific LSTM dropout accuracy pattern. General TF layer test numerical flakiness has been seen before in the investigation history.
